item.title: Career Development and Student Entrepreneurship for University-to-Work Transition in Emerging Economies
item.content:encoded:
Ugochukwu Chinonso Okolie, Leipzig University

Yuliya Shtaltovna, HS Fresenius

Paul Agu Igwe, University of Lincoln

Priscilla Bahaw, The University of the West Indies

Chibueze Tobias Orji, University of Nigeria, Nsukka

This special issue seeks empirical research on how student entrepreneurship influences the transition from university education to employment in emerging economies. The focus is on understanding how entrepreneurial experiences during higher education contribute to career development, employability skills, and readiness for labour market entry.

The call addresses a gap in research regarding student entrepreneurship's role in university-to-work transition, despite evidence that entrepreneurial activities provide experiential learning opportunities for developing workplace skills. The special issue aims to inform policymakers, university administrators, and industry experts about improving graduate employment outcomes while contributing to United Nations Sustainable Development Goals related to quality education, decent work, and reduced inequalities.

Appel publié par Career Development International. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Student Entrepreneurial Activities as a Pathway to University-to-Work Transition: exploring how students' engagement in small and micro-businesses might facilitate or hinder their transition into the labour market
  • Career Development and Employability Skills Acquisition: exploring how students' entrepreneurial engagement contributes to or hinders the development of essential employability skills and career readiness
  • Institutional and Contextual Factors in Emerging Economies: exploring how factors such as institutional support, government policies, culture and economic conditions shape student entrepreneurship and university-to-work transition outcomes
  • Cross-regional Comparative Insights & Theoretical Advancement: examining comparative perspectives on how student entrepreneurship affects university-to-work transition in different regions
  • Inner Development Goals and the Human Dimension of Entrepreneurship: integration of the IDGuide into entrepreneurship and business education, and how cognitive, social, and self-leadership competencies promote entrepreneurial behaviour and employability among students

Timeline

  • November 1, 2025: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • October 1, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Relational pedagogies in an age of GenAI
item.content:encoded:
Karen Gravett, University of Surrey

Naomi Winstone, University of Surrey

Kieran Balloo, Southern Cross University

This special issue explores relational pedagogies—teaching practices emphasizing meaningful connections between teachers and students, and engagement with both human and nonhuman entities like digital technologies—within contemporary higher education contexts shaped by generative artificial intelligence. Relational pedagogies foster emotional and affective dimensions of education while challenging competitive individualistic approaches.

The rapid emergence of GenAI is fundamentally reshaping how educators and students interact, redefining educational practices politically, practically, and ideologically. The special issue seeks critical perspectives on how GenAI reconfigures relationality in higher education, addressing questions about student engagement with AI outside educator control, evolving assessment and feedback practices, care in digitalized contexts, equity implications, and the ethical and environmental concerns these technologies raise.

Appel publié par Teaching in Higher Education. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Discourses surrounding GenAI and pedagogy
  • Relationality with respect to assessment practices
  • Relational feedback processes
  • The role of care and its connection with GenAI in contemporary universities
  • The intersection of AI technologies with notions of mattering and belonging
  • Research into academic work and relational connections
  • The materiality of education
  • Political and ethical questions regarding digital technologies such as surveillance, datafication, and agency
  • GenAI's environmental impacts and their intersection with pedagogical, ethical, and political questions
  • Posthuman, sociomaterial and feminist materialist perspectives
  • How does students' use of GenAI reshape relationships and pedagogies?
  • What role do emotions, affective relations, and embodied experiences play for students and educators in an age of GenAI?
  • How do relational pedagogic encounters with GenAI blur the boundaries between human and machine?
  • How are GenAI technologies changing relational assessment practices in higher education?
  • How are relational feedback processes evolving as a result of GenAI technologies?
  • What new methods are needed to understand our relationship with digital and GenAI technologies in higher education?
  • What questions does GenAI raise for equity perspectives on relationality?
  • What new theoretical and critical approaches are being engaged to investigate relational pedagogies and relationality in the age of GenAI?

Timeline

  • April 20, 2026: Abstract deadline
  • May 18, 2026: Expected date for abstract decisions to be communicated to authors
  • October 26, 2026: Manuscript deadline for invited draft full papers
